To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have engineered a new gene that allows the simultaneous expression and control of two different opsins in a neuron and we have used this gene to show that it is possible to control the timing of action potentials in a neuron with light.

we developed a single genetic construct that enables the optical perturbation of spike timing in neurons and that this construct may facilitate the study of the role of neural synchrony in neural computation and disease states.
we have engineered a gene which encodes two light-activated proteins, channelrhodopsins (blue light-activated cation channels) and halorhodopsins (yellow light-activated chloride pumps).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of synchrony and timing in neural computation, and how this may be manipulated in the brain using light.
the development of optogenetic techniques for the study of neural circuitry.
understanding the neural code and how it might be altered in pathological states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study provides a new and potentially useful tool to manipulate neuronal activity in vivo.
the authors have developed a novel method for manipulating the timing of neural activity.
this work demonstrates the feasibility of optogenetic perturbation of neural activity to test the role of synchrony and spike timing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of the 2A self-cleaving peptide to create a single gene encoding both channelrhodopsins and halorhodopsins can be used to control the spike timing of a neuron in a manner that is independent of the firing rate, and that this method is useful in the control of neural synchrony.
we have developed a tool to perturb spike timing, firing rate and neural synchrony.
we have developed a method to perturb the timing of neural activity in a manner that is independent of firing rate, and that can be applied to multiple cell types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now use a single gene to control the timing of action potentials in neurons with blue and yellow lights.
the use of microbial opsins can be used to manipulate neural activity in a manner that is independent of other features of the neural activity.
the combination of blue and yellow light opsins can be used to perturb the timing of spikes in a manner that is proportional to the light pulse frequency.
